text:
Dallas and Columbus meet for the second time in five days, and both arrive on a high. The Stars won the first one 3-1 on Oct. 31, then edged Washington 6-5 on the road, where Jason Robertson scored three goals in 5:20 and Mikko Rantanen reached 800 career points. They are playing without Kyle Capobianco and Oskar Bäck. The Blue Jackets beat Colorado 7-2 at home, ending the Avalanche's three-game winning streak, and both teams are 3-2-0 in their last five.

The underlying numbers lean Dallas. At five on five the Stars have taken 52% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) and Columbus 49%, and the Blue Jackets give up 3.38 expected goals per 60 minutes against Dallas's 2.69. Dallas also has the edge on special teams. In net, projected starter Jake Oettinger is 7.6 goals saved above expected this season, while projected Columbus starter Jet Greaves is at -0.8, though Greaves was +15.0 across 55 games last year. Our model has Dallas at 3.12 expected goals tonight and Columbus at 2.68.

Wyatt Johnston (38% to score) and Robertson (37%) lead our list for Dallas, and Rantanen is at 74% for a point. For Columbus, Kent Johnson has 11 points in his last 10 and a five-game point streak, and Mathieu Olivier is one goal from 50 in his career. Our under-the-radar pick is Dallas depth forward Arttu Hyry, who has produced 3.6 expected goals in his last 10 games on about 14:41 a night. We have him at 19% to score, a player to watch, not a lock.
